checks.note: a partly filled interface cell has to count as its fraction; counting it as a whole cell or as none is a whole cell of error on every surface

checks.name: surface height against the compressible prediction
checks.target: 59.8530 mm +/- 2% of the depth (filled to 60.00 mm, less 0.245% compression)

checks.name: surface flatness
checks.note: the standard deviation of the free surface over the tank; still water that is not flat is the atmospheric reconstruction pushing on it

checks.name: hydrostatic pressure gradient
checks.note: d(rho)/dz against `-rho g / c_s^2`, fitted over the fluid cells. **The most important number in this case**: pressure rising with depth at the right rate is what buoyancy IS, so a solver that gets a draft right while getting this wrong gets it right by accident. It rings acoustically for the first few hundred steps and settles; at 600 steps it read 0.94x and by 5,000 it reads 0.995x

checks.name: fluid cells touching gas cells
checks.note: the invariant the whole algorithm rests on: the interface is a closed layer one cell thick, and a hole in it means the cells around it stream in populations nothing ever wrote. A tank filled to a level that lands on a cell boundary used to produce exactly that, with no interface cells at all and a free surface that could not move

checks.name: predicted compression
checks.note: rho g h / (2 rho c_s^2) with c_s the lattice speed of sound in physical units, 10.96 m/s here
